chapters.title: What Claude Enterprise Is
chapters.tease: One identity, one Claude in every tool, and an admin plane that makes a clever assistant governable.

chapters.title: One Seat, Many Doors
chapters.tease: People meet Claude in Excel, Word, Slack, Chrome and the terminal; every door opens on one identity and one policy.

chapters.title: Team, Enterprise or the API
chapters.tease: Three ways to buy the same models; the right one is decided by who can join, who must leave and who will ask for proof.

chapters.title: The Models Behind the Seat
chapters.tease: Admins now decide which models each role may use; the task, not the leaderboard, should settle the question.

chapters.title: How Anthropic Thinks About Safety
chapters.tease: Public, dated commitments let a buyer cite what Anthropic has promised, and see clearly what it has not.

chapters.title: Per Seat, Plus Usage
chapters.tease: A flat seat plus usage at API rates makes heavy users visible, and gives admins caps and pooled budgets.

chapters.title: Five Myths About Enterprise AI
chapters.tease: The five things everyone believes about enterprise AI, and the dated record that corrects each one.

chapters.title: Decide What You Want First
chapters.tease: A one-page intent statement, signed before kickoff, separates a rollout you can judge from one you can only describe.

chapters.title: The People Who Make It Work
chapters.tease: A rollout is governed by ten named people before it is governed by any setting, and each one decides something specific.

chapters.title: Your First Thirty Days
chapters.tease: A calm first month: sign, connect, pilot one role with conservative defaults, measure, and decide at day thirty.

chapters.title: The Business Case on One Page
chapters.tease: A case written to be checked later is the only kind a controller signs twice.

chapters.title: An Inventory of Use Cases
chapters.tease: You cannot govern what you have not listed; the inventory is the first act of governance.

chapters.title: Designing a Pilot That Teaches
chapters.tease: A pilot designed to teach is useful whichever way it falls; one designed to prove is useful only once.

chapters.title: The Security Questionnaire
chapters.tease: Most questionnaire rows are already answered somewhere; the review is finding where, then doing the rest.

chapters.title: Reading the Contract
chapters.tease: The contract is a stack of promises; the reader's job is to find the clause, not the reassurance.

chapters.title: How Many Seats, and for Whom
chapters.tease: A seat count is a number; a seat plan is a roster of named groups with owners, and only the second survives finance.

chapters.title: Forecasting Usage Spend
chapters.tease: A usage forecast is a range with a guardrail; a point estimate is a wish with a decimal.

chapters.title: Buying Through a Marketplace
chapters.tease: Three doors, one building: the purchase route changes the paperwork, not the product.

chapters.title: Who Owns What
chapters.tease: A deployment owned by one team is a queue; a deployment owned along existing lines is an organisation.

chapters.title: The Go or No-Go
chapters.tease: A gate with a date, six questions and a written outcome is where judgement stays with people.

chapters.title: Single Sign-On
chapters.tease: One enforced sign-in path turns every later control, from roles to audit logs, into something you can trust.

chapters.title: Capturing the Domain
chapters.tease: The quiet accounts on your domain become one governed tenant, with each person choosing what to keep.

chapters.title: SCIM and Just-in-Time
chapters.tease: Accounts appear, change and vanish because HR and the identity provider say so, not because someone remembered.

chapters.title: Owners, Admins and Members
chapters.tease: A four-rung ladder became a set of narrow, nameable powers, so nobody needs the keys to everything.

chapters.title: Custom Roles and Groups
chapters.tease: Six roles attached to groups the identity provider already holds make joining a group the whole onboarding.

chapters.title: The Capabilities Page
chapters.tease: One quiet page of toggles is where an organisation's intentions about AI become enforceable settings.

chapters.title: Who Gets Which Model
chapters.tease: Defaults, not bans, decide what a model costs: start cheap, keep the capable model one click away.

chapters.title: The Edges of the Network
chapters.tease: A single proxy header turns the corporate network into a door for your tenant and a wall for everyone else's.

chapters.title: Devices and the Desktop App
chapters.tease: The same MDM that manages laptops can pin Claude Desktop to your tenant and fence off folders, MCP and extensions.

chapters.title: Leavers, Movers and Audits
chapters.tease: The leaver is where identity work is graded: what the data does, who inherits it, and what evidence remains.

chapters.title: What Happens to Your Data
chapters.tease: One honest page on where a prompt goes answers most of the security questionnaire before it is asked.

chapters.title: Retention You Choose
chapters.tease: Retention is three clocks and a cascade; set it deliberately and the audit log proves it ran.

chapters.title: Keys and Residency
chapters.tease: You can hold the key and pin inference to the US; both are real, both have edges, and both make you responsible.

chapters.title: Audit Logs
chapters.tease: The audit log turns every setting you chose into a record you can hand to an auditor, a court or a works council.

chapters.title: The Compliance API
chapters.tease: One API hands your security, legal and compliance tools the chats, sessions and settings they need, on request.

chapters.title: Telemetry and the SOC
chapters.tease: OpenTelemetry is the SOC's window into agentic work the endpoint agent cannot see.

chapters.title: Health Data and HIPAA
chapters.tease: A BAA is a door, not a destination: the HIPAA-ready configuration decides which features may ever touch PHI.

chapters.title: GDPR, DPIAs and the AI Act
chapters.tease: A DPIA, kept logs and informed staff satisfy most of two laws; the AI Act dates move, those duties do not.

chapters.title: A Threat Model for Assistants
chapters.tease: Four threats, one gate: injection, over-reach, supply chain and exfiltration each meet a named control.

chapters.title: Certificates and Evidence
chapters.tease: Anthropic's certificates prove its controls; only your own settings and records prove yours.

chapters.title: Projects as Shared Rooms
chapters.tease: Projects give Claude standing context with a door on it, so a team's facts live in one curated place.

chapters.title: Artifacts and Sharing
chapters.tease: Artifacts are what Claude makes; four sharing circles and two Owner switches decide how far they travel.

chapters.title: Memory and Incognito
chapters.tease: Memory is off by default for organisations, invisible to admins, and never includes what incognito chats say.

chapters.title: What a Connector Is
chapters.tease: Connectors let Claude read and act on real systems, as the signed-in person, under the permissions already there.

chapters.title: Google Workspace
chapters.tease: Three Google doors and a live-editing pane turn a calendar entry into a meeting brief in four cited calls.

chapters.title: Microsoft 365
chapters.tease: The M365 connector reaches across the tenant as the user; the risk it exposes is what SharePoint already overshares.

chapters.title: CRM, Tickets and the Rest
chapters.tease: The business systems you can connect form a cast; choose by use case, start read-only, and let the logs decide.

chapters.title: Custom Connectors via MCP
chapters.tease: Custom connectors put your own systems behind a thin MCP door, with an owner, a review and OAuth for every member.

chapters.title: Connector Policies
chapters.tease: Connector governance is five layers with five owners, from the organisation gate down to the source system.

chapters.title: Research and the Open Web
chapters.tease: Web search and Research give Claude the current world with citations; the organisation supplies the habit of checking.

chapters.title: What a Skill Is
chapters.tease: A procedure you can read, version and provision is the kind of AI an organisation can actually govern.

chapters.title: Writing a House-Style Skill
chapters.tease: The dullest skill is the one every draft needs; write it once, test it ten times and give it one owner.

chapters.title: Managing Skills Across the Organisation
chapters.tease: Three tabs, one queue and fixed versions turn a pile of department skills into something an Owner can govern.

chapters.title: Plugins and the Marketplace
chapters.tease: A plugin equips a role; a private marketplace lets the organisation decide what is stocked, for whom, in which state.

chapters.title: Trusting Third-Party Code
chapters.tease: Skills and plugins join the software supply chain; a scanner is the floor, and a human reader is still the ceiling.

chapters.title: Design, Docs and Slides
chapters.tease: Three doors that make things people edit, all drawing on one design system an Owner switches on and someone must own.

chapters.title: Templates People Actually Use
chapters.tease: A library people use is a product with a dashboard: named for the moment of need and pruned from the usage table.

chapters.title: Skills for Regulated Work
chapters.tease: Encode the checklist, the template and the playbook; keep the decision, the signature and the send with a person.

chapters.title: Owning and Retiring Skills
chapters.tease: Skills rot; a named owner, a review date and a usage number at every turn of the cycle keep them honest.

chapters.title: The Skills Catalogue
chapters.tease: Thirty folders become a system when each has a category, an owner, a risk level, its data, its audience and a number.

chapters.title: The Unified Claude
chapters.tease: One Claude replaces the chat-or-Cowork choice, and it switches itself on for existing orgs on 16 November 2026.

chapters.title: Inside the Sandbox
chapters.tease: The agent works in a throwaway VM that holds no credentials and cannot reach your network; that is the security story.

chapters.title: Network Egress
chapters.tease: One setting on one proxy is the cheapest defeat of data exfiltration by prompt injection that exists.

chapters.title: Approvals and Always Allow
chapters.tease: Classify tools, not tasks: approve reads once, click on writes, and keep sends and payments in human hands.

chapters.title: Scheduled Tasks
chapters.tease: A recurring task is a standing process with an owner, outside custom retention, that only one switch can stop.

chapters.title: Remote Control and Trusted Devices
chapters.tease: Execution stays on the member's machine while the conversation travels; Trusted Devices binds access to a known device.

chapters.title: Claude in Chrome
chapters.tease: The browser agent reaches apps without APIs and meets the open web; allowlists and two classifiers stand between.

chapters.title: Claude in Slack
chapters.tease: Claude joins channels under its own service accounts, with keys scoped per channel and results visible to all there.

chapters.title: Agents in the Office Apps
chapters.tease: Agents arrive where the numbers and the decisions live, with cell citations to check them and governance edges to know.

chapters.title: What the EDR Cannot See
chapters.tease: The endpoint agent cannot see inside the VM or cloud session, so identity, policy, telemetry and response stand in.

chapters.title: Rolling Out to Engineers
chapters.tease: Claude Code is in every seat; the rollout decides which teams absorb speed first and what gates each wave must pass.

chapters.title: Managed Settings
chapters.tease: One tier of Claude Code settings cannot be overridden by anything below it; the admin decides what lives there.

chapters.title: Heavy Users and Usage
chapters.tease: Engineering writes the usage line of the invoice; the top of the spend chart holds both your best users and your bugs.

chapters.title: Claude Security
chapters.tease: A reviewer that reads code for meaning, not just pattern, drafts the fix and leaves the decision where it belongs.

chapters.title: Review Rules for AI-Written Code
chapters.tease: The same machinery built for fallible humans, branch protection, owners and labels, keeps the merge a human decision.

chapters.title: CI and Background Agents
chapters.tease: Background agents move the code to a sandbox and the question of who is accountable back to a named person.

chapters.title: The Usage and Value Tabs
chapters.tease: Two tabs, one of counts and one of estimates with visible formulas; the second is only as honest as your inputs.

chapters.title: Onboarding a Developer
chapters.tease: A new hire has no habits; the path you give them on day one is the path the tool will actually be used on.

chapters.title: The Platform Beside the Seats
chapters.tease: Seats are for people; the platform is for software, with federated identity so the key lives nowhere.

chapters.title: Build, Buy or Wait
chapters.tease: Four answers to every 'can Claude do X', and the most interesting one, build, is the one to reach for last.

chapters.title: A Network of Champions
chapters.tease: One trusted colleague per team turns a licence purchase into a working habit, and tells you what is breaking first.

chapters.title: Training and AI Literacy
chapters.tease: The EU now requires AI literacy by law; the useful skill to teach is knowing where the model's edge is and checking.

chapters.title: Legal and Compliance Teams
chapters.tease: Two courts sanctioned invented citations and neither banned the tool; the duty to verify stays with the lawyer.

chapters.title: Finance
chapters.tease: The close is where Claude earns its seat, if the model never touches the ledger and every figure has a cell reference.

chapters.title: Sales and Customer Service
chapters.tease: The best-studied gain in AI assistance is for new support agents; the sharpest risk is customer data.

chapters.title: People Teams and Works Councils
chapters.tease: HR gains most from a policy assistant and faces the brightest legal lines; consult the council first.

chapters.title: Marketing and Communications
chapters.tease: Marketing produces the most drafts and needs three gates: a claims check, a disclosure decision and a copyright review.

chapters.title: Operations and the Public Sector
chapters.tease: Public bodies must show their working; a Project per service, a plain-English Skill and page citations let them.

chapters.title: Universities and Research
chapters.tease: A university is three organisations in one; staff adopt like any employer, students need a policy.

chapters.title: When People Push Back
chapters.tease: Pushback is information; sort the four fears by what is in your control, answer honestly, and let people opt in.

chapters.title: An AI Policy People Read
chapters.tease: A two-page policy people actually read turns a legal shield into a daily habit and the first line of evidence.

chapters.title: Spend Limits and Pooled Budgets
chapters.tease: Three nested caps and two alert thresholds turn an open-ended bill into a budget a manager can say yes to.

chapters.title: Choosing Models for Cost
chapters.tease: The model is the second biggest lever on your bill, and the right default per role is cheaper than any cap.

chapters.title: The Analytics Dashboard
chapters.tease: Five numbers a week by group, read in the same slot, give you the honest adoption story before anyone asks for it.

chapters.title: The Analytics API
chapters.tease: Owning the daily usage feed in your own warehouse turns a vendor's dashboard into your organisation's evidence.

chapters.title: Measuring Value Honestly
chapters.tease: Developers felt 20 per cent faster and measured 19 per cent slower; only baselines and holdouts tell you which you are.

chapters.title: When Something Goes Wrong
chapters.tease: AI incidents are ordinary incidents with three new places to look and two new switches, if you decided who pulls them.

chapters.title: Reviewing the Settings
chapters.tease: Defaults move under you; a quarterly settings review against the release notes is how the decisions stay yours.

chapters.title: Standards for AI Management
chapters.tease: Two standards, four functions, one filing cabinet: every Claude control gets a home and every clause gets a control.

chapters.title: The Unbothered Administrator
chapters.tease: Five verbs in a cycle, and a clear line between what you control and what you do not, is the whole practice.
